bullets.title: Weak June NFP (57K vs 110K est.) keeps Fed on hold through 2026
bullets.body: June payrolls rose just 57K, well below the 110K consensus, with prior months revised down 74K; unemployment fell to 4.2% but only on a participation drop to 61.5% (lowest since March 2021). Fed Chair Warsh said inflation risks have come down; MS Economics and market pricing now expect Fed on hold through remainder of 2026, with July hike odds falling to ~17% from ~30% pre-NFP. JPMorgan pegs first hike in September 2027 at the earliest, conditional on job or inflation upside surprises.

bullets.title: Equal-weight S&P outperforming cap-weight; breadth rally broadening
bullets.body: RSP set a fresh all-time high Thursday with equal-weight S&P outperforming cap-weighted by ~70bp on the day. MS Strategy flags median S&P 1500 stock delivering double-digit EPS growth at the fastest pace since 2021, with operating leverage strongest since then; recommends Discretionary, Transports, and Regional Banks as broadening beneficiaries. Falling crude prices and Fed on hold expected to further support the rotation away from mega-cap concentration.

bullets.title: Tech Momentum worst month since early 2000s; AI capex narrative cracking
bullets.body: MS QDS reports Tech Momentum (MSZZTMTM) down 20% MTD and -11% on Friday alone — the worst monthly reading since the early 2000s. Global Memory fell 15% and Broad AI -7.5% on the week as META's cloud compute announcement triggered profit-taking and renewed scrutiny of the AI chip-shortage thesis. AI Tech Beneficiaries saw ~3z net selling Thursday, the largest single-day net reduction on record.

bullets.title: HF de-grossing underway; tech crowding at extremes sets up further unwind
bullets.body: JPM Prime notes HF gross leverage peaked post-June expiry at 92nd percentile on a 12-month basis and 98th on a 5-year basis; early de-grossing flows emerged over three North America sessions (6/29–7/1) with seasonal history pointing to more into late July. Mag 7 and Software were sold at -2z each in June, with positioning now at just the 16th and 11th percentiles respectively. US momentum factor is already down ~17% from its June 22 peak.

bullets.title: Weekly tape: Nasdaq +2.12% led by big tech; SOX -4.4% worst performer
bullets.body: For the week, Nasdaq gained 2.12%, S&P +1.76%, Dow +1.97%, while Russell 2000 lagged at -0.46%. AAPL +8.8%, GOOGL +6.7%, META +5.9% drove large-cap tech; IGV (software) added 6.1% but SOX (semis/memory) fell 4.4%. Thursday's session was mixed with S&P flat, Nasdaq -0.80%, and Dow +1.14% as semis and memory gave back gains on AI capex scrutiny.

bullets.title: META cloud compute launch disrupts AI-chip-shortage narrative; Bitcoin miners hit
bullets.body: META's reported plan to sell external compute capacity and AI model access triggered a broad re-rating of the AI supply-scarcity trade. Bitcoin miners fell >20% on skepticism over compute shortages, and the move sparked the largest single-day AI Tech net selling on record per MS QDS. JPM credit views the launch as supportive of META's capex discipline and monetization, noting no current evidence of overbuild.

bullets.title: Q2 S&P 500 EPS growth tracking 20%+; Normal expansion regime intact
bullets.body: FactSet expects 23.3% y/y S&P 500 EPS growth in Q2, which would be the second consecutive 20%+ quarter. 22V Research's macro regime model classifies the environment as Normal expansion driven by sales growth and margin expansion; consensus 2026 S&P EPS sits at $343, +14.5% y/y. Credit spreads at tightest since 1984 are flagged as an outlier to normalize gradually rather than signal downturn.

bullets.title: Semis short gamma elevated; levered ETF exposure near historical highs
bullets.body: MS QDS reports levered ETF short gamma at -$16bn per 1% move, near historical highs, with SK Hynix and Micron carrying the highest short gamma in the book. SOX rallied +87.8% in Q2, making historically elevated exposures increasingly difficult to sustain per MS Strategy. Retail investors were net buyers of $36bn in equities last week (89th percentile), $22bn via single stocks, providing some offset.

bullets.title: IGV down 14% YTD vs S&P +10%; SaaS valuations at 5.3x FY+2 EV/Sales
bullets.body: Wolfe's Zukin flags that IGV is down 14.3% YTD versus S&P 500 up 10.1%, with the Apps subsector leading the decline in June. All-SaaS index trades at 5.3x FY+2 EV/Sales and Security at 8.3x; Wolfe is long MDB, DDOG, SNOW, PANW, and NOW on AI tailwinds, citing 30%+ Atlas growth at MDB and strong DDOG GPU consumption checks.

bullets.title: Regional banks benefit from 'hawkish hold'; rate-hike window pushed to December
bullets.body: Soft employment data pushed full hike expectations from October to December, a net positive for regional banks as the belly of the curve fell 4-6bp and funding costs stay muted. KRE has been down only 5 of the last 22 trading days since June 1; RBC is bullish on US Banks citing loan growth, NII acceleration, M&A momentum, and Basel III endgame. Key monitor: core PCE at 0.21% or below keeps Fed at bay.

bullets.title: Oil at ~$70/bbl post-Iran deal; gasoline still 28% above pre-conflict US levels
bullets.body: Brent crude fell from $120/bbl in April to ~$70/bbl following the US-Iran deal in mid-June, with JPMorgan now forecasting $80/bbl average for 2H26. Despite crude returning to pre-conflict levels, US gasoline remains 28% above pre-conflict prices and jet fuel lags; energy cost relief is filtering through to consumer confidence but not yet fully to pump prices. Lower energy is expected to be a meaningful tailwind for the broadening equity rally.

bullets.title: Euro area growth revised up; ECB one more hike in September as core stays at 2.4%
bullets.body: JPMorgan raised 4Q26-2Q27 Euro area GDP to 1.5% annualized (from 1.3%) as the Middle East energy drag fades. Headline inflation fell to 2.8% YoY in June, core to 2.4%, but core is expected to re-accelerate to 2.5% by 4Q26 before declining — supporting one final ECB hike in September with risks skewed toward 'one-and-done.' Bank lending accelerated to 3.5% YoY and ESI rose 1.3pt to 95.0.

bullets.title: USD bullishness intact; EM Asia most vulnerable to Fed, LatAm less exposed
bullets.body: JPMorgan's FX strategy team increased USD bullishness citing US exceptionalism in yields, equity returns, and growth; nine FOMC members now project hikes this year. Vietnam is flagged as most acutely vulnerable in Asia Edge given ongoing capital outflows, trade balance deterioration, and direct linkage to US monetary policy. Latin America is less exposed due to lower inflation; Europe Edge is least exposed of EM regions.

bullets.title: USMCA moves to annual review; Mexico nearshoring advantage intact near-term
bullets.body: The US formally declined USMCA renewal at the July 1 deadline but kept the treaty in force, shifting to an annual review process through 2036. Mexico retains its trade advantage in pharma, semiconductors, and advanced manufacturing; the next bilateral negotiation round is scheduled for the week of July 20 to address auto content rules (82% North American, 50% US-specific), transshipment controls, and trade deficits.

bullets.title: Global capex nowcast at 9.8% annualized in 2Q; EM capex running at 17%
bullets.body: JPMorgan's capex nowcaster shows 2Q26 global capex at 9.8% annualized — moderating from prior trend but still robust, supported by investment goods PMI rising to 54.1 from 51.8 in 1Q. Capital goods IP accelerated to 10.0% in 2Q from 5.4% in 1Q. Emerging market capex is tracking 17.0% annualized, down modestly from 18.5% in 1Q, remaining the strongest growth pocket globally.

bullets.title: Apple cuts iPhone 17 production 15%; memory supply crunch adds cost pressure
bullets.body: Apple reduced iPhone 17 production by ~15% as demand normalizes, while simultaneously ramping foldable iPhone production to 10M units on what analysts flag as optimistic forecasts. Memory shortages are driving cost pressures; Apple is reportedly in talks to source chips from Chinese suppliers on the Pentagon blacklist and lobbying the White House for political cover, creating a national security overhang.

bullets.title: TSLA Q2 deliveries 480K+, +34% q/q and +25% y/y; beat but bar flagged as elevated
bullets.body: Tesla reported Q2 deliveries exceeding 480K, beating the ~406K consensus by a wide margin and up 34% sequentially and 25% year-over-year. Analysts cautioned that buy-side expectations had been reset higher into the print, limiting the upside reaction from the headline beat.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler implied vol at multi-year highs; upside calls skewed vs ATM
bullets.body: 22V Research notes 6-month implied volatility on hyperscalers is at multi-year highs with upside calls richly skewed versus ATM options, creating what they describe as a low-cost overlay entry point for a H2 rebound. AI-related exports represent roughly half of China's total export growth, and the US semiconductor export controls vs. Chinese rare earth restrictions truce is flagged as increasingly fragile as Chinese AI models gain US market share.

bullets.title: Consumer confidence rising on lower gasoline; retail traffic decelerating into Q2
bullets.body: PSC Macro's daily consumer confidence tracker is rising as gasoline prices decline, with both investor and non-investor components trending up. However, KeyBanc geolocation data shows Q2 hardlines traffic broadly decelerating vs Q1 — Walmart slowed 190bp to +0.8%, Home Depot -160bp to -0.5%, Lowe's -250bp to -0.7% — with only Musa and Best Buy accelerating quarter-over-quarter.

bullets.title: Cruise lines down 5-8% on Iran conflict / airlift concerns; WYNN Vegas estimates cut
bullets.body: Cruise lines (CCL, RCL, NCLH) declined 5-8% on cancellation and spending uncertainty tied to Iran conflict and lower airlift into resort markets. UBS separately cut WYNN Q2 Vegas revenue to $637M (flat YoY) from $645M as Harry Reid airport passenger volume fell 7-8% YoY on Spirit bankruptcy-driven capacity reduction; Macau June GGR was down 12% YoY with World Cup impact fading post-July 19.
